## Decode same-color corner cells from a striped lattice (task `task-58b9cfe0`, verified correct)

A regular wallpaper grid has horizontal and vertical separator stripes (often alternating with uniform rectangular interiors). At selected intersections of the stripes, the separator-color pixels are replaced by colors encoding lattice vertices. Find the rectangular subgrid of these changed intersection points (the active/encoded patch); retain the ordered consecutive horizontal and vertical intersection coordinates spanning it. Output one cell for each adjacent pair of lattice rows and adjacent pair of lattice columns. For each resulting rectangle, if all four corner intersection values are the same, output that color; otherwise output the uniform interior/background color from the original repeating pattern. Verified task test: 27x27 pattern with separator rows y=0,4,8,12,16,20,24 and separator columns x=4,9,14,19,24. Encoded intersection patch was y=4,8,12,16,20,24 and x=9,14,19,24. Interior/default color was 3. Applying the all-four-corners-equal rule gave the accepted 5x3 output:
